expectations.text: Rejects assuming attendance falls when an event goes virtual as a planning default.
expectations.evidence: 'The published evidence doesn't support "people show up less."'

expectations.text: Cites PyCon US counting about 22% fewer people in 2021 as a virtual event, roughly 2,650, than the 3,393 checked in at the in-person 2019 edition.
expectations.evidence: Table: 3,393 to about 2,650, about 22% fewer.

expectations.text: Cites KubeCon+CloudNativeCon North America registrations nearly doubling the other way, from 11,891 in 2019 in-person to 22,816 or more in 2020 virtual.
expectations.evidence: 11,891 to 22,816+ registrations.

expectations.text: States that removing travel cost and geography can grow the number as easily as losing the room shrinks it.
expectations.evidence: 'can grow the audience as easily as losing the room shrinks it.'

expectations.text: Recommends planning capacity from this event's own signals rather than from either direction as a default.
expectations.evidence: 'Build the base case from this event's own signals'.

expectations.text: Rejects the hybrid cost breakdown as a baseline, stating it prices a hybrid run's virtual layer and not a standalone virtual production.
expectations.evidence: 'prices the virtual layer of a hybrid run, not a standalone virtual event.'

expectations.text: Recommends asking the platform vendor the concurrent-viewer ceiling on the plan being bought, in writing.
expectations.evidence: 'Ask the vendor in writing what happens at the ceiling'; the ceiling is among the written questions.

expectations.text: Recommends asking what happens at that ceiling: a queue, a refusal, or an upgrade invoice.
expectations.evidence: 'a queue, a refusal, or an upgrade invoice.'

expectations.text: Hands the cost consequence to samber/dev-event-organizer-skills@event-budget rather than producing the budget here.

expectations.text: Splits that cost by what a lean tier drops, stating the feed itself survives every tier while the interaction surface and its staffing go first.
